title: rsync for sync
intro: Work from the module directory. Parse **`rsync_dryrun.txt`** and **`rsync_merge.txt`** unless noted.

questions.prompt: In **`rsync_dryrun.txt`**, how many files are scheduled for **deletion** from the destination? Print **only** the integer.
From those **`*deleting`** lines, print the **basename** only (after the last **`/`**), **one per line**, sorted in **ASCII** order.
How many **regular file transfers** (not deletions or directory changes) are listed? Print **only** the integer.
Print the **full relative path** from each **`>f`** line (path after the 11-character itemize code and its space), **one per line**, sorted in ASCII order.
questions.solutionMarkdown: Strip the itemize prefix from **`>f…`** lines, then **`sort`**.

questions.prompt: How many of the transferred files are being **created for the first time** on the destination — i.e. all transfer attributes are new? Print **only** the integer.
How many **directory creations** appear in the dry-run output? Print **only** the integer.

Using **`rsync_merge.txt`** (merge semantics: **`+`** / **`-`**, **`*`** does not cross **`/`**, first match wins): would **`server.log`** at the **transfer root** be included? Answer **`YES`** or **`NO`** only.
Same rules: would **`nested/server.log`** be included? Answer **`YES`** or **`NO`** only.
In **two or three sentences**, explain the layout difference between **`rsync -a src/ dest/`** and **`rsync -a src dest/`** when **`src`** is a directory.
questions.expectedOutput: rsync -a src/ dest/ copies the contents of src into dest, so files land directly under dest/. rsync -a src dest/ copies the directory src as a whole, creating dest/src/.... The trailing slash on the source controls whether the destination receives a mirror of the folder's contents or a new subdirectory named like the source.

questions.prompt: In **three to five sentences**, contrast **`--delete`**, **`--delete-before`**, **`--delete-after`**, and **`--delete-delayed`**, and why **`--dry-run`** matters before any delete mode.
questions.expectedOutput: --delete removes files in the destination that are absent from the source so the destination converges to the source's shape; --delete-before does those deletes before new data is written (good for freeing space, risky if the run stops early); --delete-after deletes extras after the main file updates (old junk lingers longer); --delete-delayed batches deletes to run late in the transfer, deferring most removals until later in the run. All of them can destroy data if SRC/DEST are reversed, so rsync -n with identical arguments is mandatory before a real delete run.
questions.solutionMarkdown: Summarize timing of deletes vs transfers from **`answers.md`**.

summaryMarkdown:
## Learning outcomes
- Use trailing slash semantics (`src/` vs `src`) to control directory contents vs directory node.
- Apply include/exclude filters (`--include`, `--exclude`, `--filter`).
- Interpret `--dry-run` output before destructive `--delete` variants.
- Choose checksum vs size/mtime for change detection (`-c` cost).

## Scope

**In scope:** local and over-SSH sync in lab. **Out of scope:** `rsync` daemon mode in production.

## Concept outline

1. **Basic invocations** — `-a` archive bits, `-v`, `-h`, `-z` compression trade-off on fast LAN.
2. **Deletes** — `--delete`, `--delete-delayed`, `--backup` + `--backup-dir`.
3. **Partial / resume** — `--partial`, `--inplace` risks; `rsync` 3.2+ features if available.
4. **Remote** — `rsync -e "ssh -i …" user@host:path/`.
5. **macOS** — bundled `rsync` age vs Homebrew modern `rsync` (feature gaps).

## Tooling and alternatives

| Task | Primary | Alternatives |
|------|---------|----------------|
| Directory sync | `rsync` | `cp -a` (no delete/sync semantics), `tar` pipeline **13** (`tar cf - src \| ssh … tar xf -`), `zsync` (HTTP), `rclone` (multi-backend cloud). |
| Two-way sync | `rsync` one-way per direction | `unison`, `syncthing` GUIs; **not** `rsync` alone. |
| Byte-level diff large files | `rsync --inplace` | `zsync`, `rdiff-backup`, `borg` for versioned backups. |
| Mirror HTTP | N/A | `wget` (**20**), `lftp mirror`. |
